distinguishing_features: Pins ice nucleation to a fixed micro-textured lamella array rather than pulsing existing recirculation flow
Decouples nucleation site from crystal-growth/shear environment via flow-field-segregated stationary high-shear zones
Uses shear-induced detachment of ice crystals (tau_s > sigma_a) to prevent thick ice growth rather than disrupting crud precipitation kinetics
Adds a micro-lamella heat exchanger replacement rather than modulating an existing pump/temperature duty cycle
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to prevent a growing ice layer from trapping solute and insulating the heat-transfer surface during freeze-concentration, by continuously removing ice before it accumulates rather than by suppressing or thermally disrupting nucleation.
parsed.viable_reason: Microchannel high-shear flow with shear stress exceeding estimated ice adhesion (~5-15 Pa vs ~10 Pa) to shear off thin ice is physically plausible and testable at the stated 100 micron scale, consistent with ice-slurry/suspension freeze-concentration art.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Unlike prior art 1's pulse/temperature cycling on existing hardware, pinning nucleation to a fixed micro-textured array while segregating the shear-detachment zone is a distinct flow-configuration mechanism, not a routine parameter change to the closest art.
